decisions.reason: It is the firm's publicly announced flagship, shown on the home page and central to its stated direction, so dropping it would write off a visible investment and expose the strategic choice as a mistake.
Its dedicated page signals meaningful investment and visible commitment, and any weak early results can still be attributed to ramp-up in the document workflow market.
It builds on the core messaging infrastructure at low incremental cost and serves regulated customers who still rely on fax, so there is little reason to withdraw it this early.
It is a low-visibility feature close to the core offer, so dropping it would cost little, but it costs little to keep and supports existing fax customers.
Sandbox protection supports the firm's security positioning and growing threat-protection demand, which justifies the R&D already invested.
It involves little public commitment, but as an integrated part of the email security suite it is cheap to keep and too early to judge as failed.
